summary: This bill makes Executive Order 13989 on ethics commitments by executive branch personnel have the force and effect of law.

scores.thoughts: The bill codifies an executive order on ethics commitments for executive branch personnel. It contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or spending levels.
The bill addresses ethics rules for executive officials and has no provisions concerning tax rates, tax policy, or revenue collection.
No content in the bill relates to healthcare delivery, insurance, public programs, or market-based reforms.
The legislation is silent on firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration pathways, border enforcement, or related protections.
The bill does not engage with reproductive rights or abortion access in any way.
No references to defense budgets, military policy, or national security spending appear in the text.
The bill contains nothing related to environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net policies.
The legislation does not address schools, federal education funding, or school choice.
No content pertains to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
The bill focuses solely on ethics commitments and does not touch sentencing, policing, or justice reform.
No provisions relate to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No language concerns legal protections or restrictions based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
The legislation contains no references to foreign assistance or international aid.
Nothing in the bill pertains to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
The bill does not engage with technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The bill is limited to ethics commitments and does not address religious exemptions or civil rights priorities.
